correctness.rationale: If the split leaf has depth d and cherry indicator I, the increments are 1−I, d+2, and 2(d+1)−2Id for K, S, and Q. The last identity adds the two new leaves and removes the old pair only when I=1. Uniform sampling gives conditional means E[I]=2K/n, E[d]=S/n, E[Id]=Q/n. Writing D=Q−2S/3 leads directly to E[D_{n+1}|T_n]=(1−2/n)D_n+2/3 and hence E[D_n]=2n/9 from D_3=2/3. The mean recursions similarly give E[K_n]=n/3 and E[S_n]=2n(H_n−1) from (K_3,S_3)=(1,5). In the law of total covariance, the conditional covariance is −Q/n+2KS/n², and the covariance of conditional means is (1−2/n)(1+1/n) times the old covariance. Combining terms cancels 2/n² in the coefficient and leaves v_{n+1}=(1−1/n)v_n−2/9. From v_3=0, telescoping gives (n−1)v_n=−[n(n−1)−6]/9. The sign, asymptotic and deterministic n=2 case follow. The sentence that the new cherry is two levels below the old parent is a prose slip: the new parent is at d, one edge below the old parent; the new leaves are two edges below that parent. The proof uses the correct depths.
residual_risks: Source checker was read, not run. Its finite weighted shape enumeration and recurrence calculations corroborate rather than prove the all-size result.

evidence: The random-permutation BST formula, for m stored keys, is Cov(L_m,P_m)=−(m−2)(m+3)/(9m). Cardona et al. describe the equivalent equal-rates Markov/Yule tree convention.
equivalent_formulations.reasoning: Adjoin the null children of the BST as external leaves. The next insertion picks a gap uniformly conditional on the relative insertion order, which is uniform leaf splitting. The resulting n=m+1 external-leaf tree has cherries exactly at the BST leaf keys. Its Sackin sum is the external path length, equal to the internal path length plus 2m. Thus the prior BST covariance is exactly the frozen Yule expression, not just a comparable shape measure.

evidence: The October 13 record states −n/9+2/[3(n−1)] and E[Q_n]=(2/3)E[S_n]+2n/9; the October 18 record states the same covariance. The November 2 record also gives both identities but postdates the frozen finding.
exact_database_or_table.reasoning: These are exact all-size formulas, not finite table coincidences. Expanding (n−3)(n+2)=n(n−1)−6 and inserting E[S_n]=2n(H_n−1) verifies exact identity with the October 13 statement. The later result is collateral overlap, not evidence of earlier priority.

value.rationale: The covariance and depth moment are worthwhile exact measures of Yule tree shape in isolation. As a new finding this record supplies no useful increment: both are already given together with the same recurrence, and the circulated BST and root-split forms give equivalent coverage of the main statistic. Finite rechecking of these exact identities does not make a distinct result.
residual_risks: This assessment is about the frozen contribution, not the usefulness of these mixed moments generally.
